questions.question: A car travels four consecutive distances of 2 km each at speeds of 10 km/hr, 20 km/hr, 30 km/hr, and 40 km/hr, respectively. What is the average speed of the car (in km/hr) over this total distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal consecutive distances, the average speed is independent of the actual distance length.

Assume the distance of each part = LCM(10, 20, 30, 40) = 120 km.

Total distance = 4 parts × 120 km = 480 km.

Total time taken = (120÷10) + (120÷20) + (120÷30) + (120÷40) = 12 + 6 + 4 + 3 = 25 hours.

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 480 ÷ 25 = 19.2 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of each consecutive part = 2 km.

Speeds for each respective part = 10 km/hr, 20 km/hr, 30 km/hr, 40 km/hr.

 
 
•

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 km

⇒ Time for 1st part = 2 ÷ 10 = 1/5 hr

⇒ Time for 2nd part = 2 ÷ 20 = 1/10 hr

⇒ Time for 3rd part = 2 ÷ 30 = 1/15 hr

⇒ Time for 4th part = 2 ÷ 40 = 1/20 hr

⇒ Total Time = 1/5 + 1/10 + 1/15 + 1/20

⇒ LCM of denominators (5, 10, 15, 20) is 60.

⇒ Total Time = (12 + 6 + 4 + 3) ÷ 60 = 25/60 = 5/12 hr

⇒ Average Speed = 8 ÷ (5/12)

⇒ Average Speed = (8 × 12) ÷ 5 = 96 ÷ 5 = 19.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed General Formula

Average Speed is always calculated as Total Distance divided by Total Time. Never take the arithmetic mean of the individual speeds unless the time intervals spent traveling at each speed are equal.

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If an object covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the harmonic mean: Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If an object covers three equal consecutive distances at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is calculated as: Average Speed = (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).
</p

questions.question: Avi can finish a piece of work in 6 days, Avni can finish it in 8 days, Aarti can do it in 12 days and Reeta can do it in 16 days. They all decided to work one by one, Avi starts the work and works for one-fourth of a day, then Avni works for one-fourth of a day, then Aarti works for one-fourth of a day and then Reeta works for the remaining one-fourth of a day. Efficiencies: Avi = 8, Avni = 6, Aarti = 4, Reeta = 3.

Work per cycle (each works 1/4 day) = (8 + 6 + 4 + 3) × 1/4 = 21/4 = 5.25 units.

Work done in 9 complete cycles = 9 × 5.25 = 47.25 units.

Remaining work = 48 − 47.25 = 0.75 units.

The next turn is Avi's (capacity = 2 units/turn). Since 0.75 units [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by Avi in 1/4 day = 8 × 1/4 = 2 units

⇒ Work done by Avni in 1/4 day = 6 × 1/4 = 1.5 units

⇒ Work done by Aarti in 1/4 day = 4 × 1/4 = 1 unit

⇒ Work done by Reeta in 1/4 day = 3 × 1/4 = 0.75 units

⇒ Total work completed in 1 cycle (1 full day) = 2 + 1.5 + 1 + 0.75 = 5.25 units

⇒ Number of complete cycles nearest to 48 units = 48 ÷ 5.25 ≈ 9.14 ⇒ 9 cycles

⇒ Since the remaining 0.75 units is less than 2 units, Avi completes the entire remaining work.

**∴ The correct answer is Avi.**

Time & Work (LCM Method)

Total work is assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times to simplify fraction calculations. Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Alternate Work Concept

When individuals work in a sequence, always calculate the combined work for one full cycle. Find the maximum number of full cycles that fit into the total work before systematically evaluating the remaining work sequence by sequence to find the exact finisher.

questions.question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 198 and 9 respectively. If one of the numbers is 99, then find the other number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the property: First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

99 × Second Number = 198 × 9

Second Number = (198 × 9) ÷ 99

Second Number = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 198

HCF of two numbers = 9

First Number = 99

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

**Calculations:**

⇒ 99 × Second Number = 198 × 9

⇒ Second Number = (198 × 9) ÷ 99

⇒ Second Number = 198 ÷ 99 × 9

⇒ Second Number = 2 × 9

⇒ Second Number = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between LCM and HCF

The product of the LCM and HCF of any two given natural numbers is strictly equal to the product of the given numbers. The formula is: LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂.

HCF and LCM of Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is exactly 1. Because of this, the LCM of two co-prime numbers will always be their direct product.

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators.
HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.
</p

questions.question: A refinery produces 3 grades of gasoline: Regular (85% octane), Mid-grade (90% octane), and Premium (95% octane). If 200 barrels of Regular, 100 barrels of Mid-grade, and 100 barrels of Premium are mixed, what is the average octane rating?

Ratio of quantities = 200 : 100 : 100 = 2 : 1 : 1.

Let the assumed average be 90%.

Actual Average = 90% − 1.25% = 88.75%.

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹45, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1 year = ₹40 ÷ 2 = ₹20.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = ₹45 − ₹40 = ₹5.

This difference of ₹5 is the interest generated on the 1st year's SI.

Rate (R) = (Difference ÷ 1st year SI) × 100 = (5 ÷ 20) × 100 = 25%.

Principal (P) = (1st year SI × 100) ÷ R = (20 × 100) ÷ 25 = ₹80.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = 2 years, Simple Interest (SI) = ₹40, Compound Interest (CI) = ₹45.

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (R ÷ 100)²

 
 SI vs CI Tree Diagram for 2 Years
 
 
 
• 
 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 2 years = (P × R × 2) ÷ 100 = 40

⇒ (P × R) ÷ 100 = 20 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ Difference in interests for 2 years (CI − SI) = 45 − 40 = 5

⇒ P × (R ÷ 100)² = 5

⇒ [ (P × R) ÷ 100 ] × (R ÷ 100) = 5

⇒ Substituting Equation 1 into the above relationship:

⇒ 20 × (R ÷ 100) = 5

⇒ R = (5 × 100) ÷ 20 = 25%

⇒ Now, substituting R = 25% back into Equation 1:

⇒ (P × 25) ÷ 100 = 20

⇒ P × (1 ÷ 4) = 20

⇒ P = 20 × 4 = ₹80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

For a principal P and rate R% for 2 years, Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

For a principal P and rate R% for 3 years, Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × [(R ÷ 100) + 3].

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the effective rate becomes (R ÷ 2) and the number of periods becomes (2T).

Rule of 72

A quick mental math trick to estimate the time required to double an investment at a given compound interest rate: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.

questions.question: Rupesh has two grandsons Mandar and Ketan. 13 year old Mandar gets some money from Rupesh’s wealth and 14 year old Ketan gets rest of the money. But Mandar and Ketan will get money only when they turn 23 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 5% compounded annually. When both turn 23, they receive the same amount. How much had Rupesh given Ketan (in ₹) initially, if total money with Rupesh was ₹24600?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for Mandar = 23 − 13 = 10 years, Time for Ketan = 23 − 14 = 9 years.

Difference in time = 10 − 9 = 1 year.

Since final amounts are equal, the ratio of their shares (Ketan : Mandar) = (100 + R)/100 = 105/100 = 21 : 20.

Ketan's share = [21 / (21 + 20)] × 24600 = (21 / 41) × 24600 = 21 × 600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total money given by Rupesh = ₹24600

Rate of interest (R) = 5% compounded annually

Age of Mandar = 13 years, Age of Ketan = 14 years

Target age for receiving money = 23 years

 
 Mandar (₹M)
 13 → 23 yrs (10 years)
 Amt: A

 
 Ketan (₹K)
 14 → 23 yrs (9 years)
 Amt: A

 Total Amount = M + K = ₹24600
 M × (1.05)¹⁰ = K × (1.05)⁹

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial amount given to Mandar be M and to Ketan be K.

⇒ Total money = M + K = 24600

⇒ Time duration for Mandar = 23 − 13 = 10 years

⇒ Time duration for Ketan = 23 − 14 = 9 years

⇒ As per the question, the amount received by both at age 23 is equal.

⇒ M × (1 + 5/100)¹⁰ = K × (1 + 5/100)⁹

⇒ M × (105/100)¹⁰ = K × (105/100)⁹

⇒ K / M = 105 / 100 = 21 / 20

⇒ Ratio of Ketan's share to Mandar's share = 21 : 20

⇒ Total ratio parts = 21 + 20 = 41 parts

⇒ 41 parts = 24600

⇒ 1 part = 24600 ÷ 41 = 600

⇒ Ketan's share = 21 parts = 21 × 600 = 12600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

Amount A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and n is the time period in years.

Division of Wealth Based on CI

When a sum is divided such that two parts amount to the same value after t₁ and t₂ years, their initial amounts are inversely proportional to (1 + R/100)time. The part invested for fewer years will require a larger initial principal to reach the same final amount.

Effective Multiplying Factor

For compound interest, the principal grows by a constant multiplying factor every year, which equates to (100 + R)/100. For a 5% rate, this factor is exactly 1.05 or 21/20.

A = √(4 × 48 × 48) = 2 × 48 = 96

**∴ The correct answer is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A / 192 = 48 / A

**Calculation:**

By cross-multiplying the terms on both sides:

⇒ A × A = 192 × 48

⇒ A² = (48 × 4) × 48

⇒ A² = 48² × 4

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ A = √(48² × 2²)

⇒ A = 48 × 2

⇒ A = 96

**∴ The correct answer is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication

When solving linear equations with equivalent fractions on both sides, cross-multiplying (multiplying the numerator of one side by the denominator of the other) directly yields an integer equation: a/b = c/d ⇒ a × d = b × c.

Simplifying Square Roots

Instead of multiplying large numbers to evaluate a perfect square, breaking the values down into prime factors and creating equivalent pairs helps calculate the root considerably faster. Using the property √(x² × y²) = x × y.
</p

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a weight that actually weighs 32% less than what is written on it. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the claimed weight be 100 units.

Since the goods are sold at cost price, Selling Price (SP) = 100 units.

Actual weight given to the customer = 100 − 32 = 68 units.

Cost Price (CP) for the shopkeeper = 68 units.

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = (32 ÷ 68) × 100 = 800 ÷ 17 = 47 ¹/₁₇ %.

**∴ The correct answer is 47 ¹/₁₇ %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price.

He uses a weight that is 32% less than the marked weight.

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = (Claimed Weight − Actual Weight) ÷ Actual Weight × 100

 
 Claimed Weight = 100 units (SP)
 
 
 Actual Weight = 68 units (CP)
 
 
 Profit = 32
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Profit % = (32 ÷ 68) × 100 ≈ 47.05%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the true marked weight be 1000 g.

⇒ False actual weight = 1000 − (32% of 1000) = 1000 − 320 = 680 g.

⇒ Since he sells at CP, he charges for 1000 g but gives only 680 g.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) for the shopkeeper = Cost of 680 g.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for the shopkeeper = Cost of 1000 g.

⇒ Profit made = 1000 − 680 = 320 g equivalent.

⇒ Profit % = (320 ÷ 680) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (8 ÷ 17) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 800 ÷ 17 = 47 ¹/₁₇ %

**∴ The correct answer is 47 ¹/₁₇ %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer (Selling at CP)

When a shopkeeper sells goods at cost price but uses a false weight, his Profit % is calculated directly as (Error ÷ True Weight Given) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer (Selling at Profit/Loss)

If the dealer marks up the price and also cheats on weight, the overall ratio is SP ÷ CP = (Claimed Weight ÷ Actual Weight) × (Price Charged ÷ Actual Price).

Successive Changes

To calculate the net effect of two successive percentage changes A% and B%, use the net change formula: A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100.
</p

questions.question: The average age of 48 students of a class is 10 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 11 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Teacher's age = New Average + (Number of old members × Increase in average)

⇒ Teacher's age = 11 + (48 × 1)

⇒ Teacher's age = 11 + 48 = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 48

Average age of students = 10 years

New average age after including the teacher = 11 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of Persons

 
 
 

 
 

 
 48 Students (Avg 10)
 Total = 48 × 10 = 480

 
 + 1 Teacher
 Age = ?

 
• 

 
 49 Persons (New Avg 11)
 Total = 49 × 11 = 539

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 48 students = 48 × 10 = 480 years

⇒ Total members after including the teacher = 48 + 1 = 49

⇒ Total age of 49 members = 49 × 11 = 539 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = Total age of 49 members − Total age of 48 students

⇒ Age of the teacher = 539 − 480 = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes N₁ and N₂ are combined, the new combined average is calculated as (N₁ × A₁ + N₂ × A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂).

Replacement in Averages

If a person is replaced and the average increases by a value 'd', the new person's value is equal to: Old person's value + (Total number of persons × d).

Exclusion from Averages

If a person leaves the group and the average decreases by a value 'd', the leaving person's value is equal to: Old Average + (Remaining persons × d).
</p

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 12, 28, 36 and 27 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the smallest number divisible by 12, 28, 36, and 27, calculate their LCM.

Since 36 is a multiple of 12, we can omit 12 and directly find the LCM of 28, 36, and 27.

LCM of 36 (4 × 9) and 27 (3 × 9) is 108.

Now, LCM of 108 and 28 (which is 4 × 7) is 108 × 7 = 756.

**∴ The correct answer is 756.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 12, 28, 36, and 27.

**Method Used:**

The smallest natural number completely divisible by a given set of numbers is their Lowest Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 27 = 3³

⇒ The prime factors present in all given numbers are 2, 3, and 7.

⇒ The highest power of 2 is 2² = 4

⇒ The highest power of 3 is 3³ = 27

⇒ The highest power of 7 is 7¹ = 7

⇒ LCM = Product of the highest powers of all prime factors

⇒ LCM = 4 × 27 × 7

⇒ LCM = 108 × 7

⇒ LCM = 756

**∴ The correct answer is 756.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest non-zero number that is a multiple of all the given numbers. It is found by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that divides all the given numbers completely. It is found by multiplying the lowest powers of common prime factors.

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

For any two positive integers a and b: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b). This rule strictly applies to pairs of numbers only.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their direct product.
</p

questions.question: The population of a district is 385000, out of which 168000 are males. 52% of the population is literate. If 21% males are literate, then what percentage of females are literate?

Total population = 385,000, Males = 168,000 ⇒ Females = 217,000

Ratio of Male to Female = 168,000 : 217,000 = 24 : 31

Using the Alligation method on literacy rates:

(Female % − 52%) ÷ (52% − 21%) = Male Ratio ÷ Female Ratio = 24 ÷ 31

⇒ (Female % − 52%) ÷ 31% = 24 ÷ 31 ⇒ Female % − 52% = 24% ⇒ Female % = 76%

**∴ The correct answer is 76%.**
